name: Vodyanitsa
title: Lingering Siren-Song
description: Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe and a Water Imp who has parted from her kin.

skills.name: Psyshkhwe Arietta
skills.description:
Normal Attack
Sings an ancient song of the Water Imps, unleashing up to 4 strikes. This deals Hydro DMG to the opponent.

Charged Attack
Consumes a certain amount of Stamina to hurl a water ball forward, dealing Hydro DMG.

Plunging Attack
Plunges towards the ground from mid-air, damaging all opponents along the path. Deals AoE Hydro DMG upon impact with the ground.

skills.name: Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn
skills.description:
Reveals her true Water Imp form, dealing AoE Hydro DMG and gaining the Song of Ages Past effect: While this effect is active, Vodyanitsa summons the ancient Horn of Spring's Call, periodically moving closer to an opponent in a swift movement to attack them, dealing Hydro DMG.
The above two types of attacks will also decrease the Hydro RES and Cryo RES of opponents hit. Additionally, while the Song of Ages Past effect is active, the party's active character gains increased resistance to interruption and periodically regenerates HP based on Vodyanitsa's Max HP.

attributes.label: Horn of Spring's Call Attack Interval
Song of Ages Past Healing Interval

skills.name: Koda: Sink With Thee
skills.description:
Leads a song of the Water Imps which lures its listeners to their doom. This deals AoE Hydro DMG to the opponent.
When in the Song of Ages Past state, DMG dealt is further increased.

attributes.label: Song of Ages Past DMG Bonus

passives.name: The Last Djeguako Songstress
passives.description:
When the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn is used, any Stellar Vortex on the field will turn into a Wandering Vortex instead. While the Song of Ages Past effect is active, nearby party members' Stellar Swirl reactions will generate Wandering Vortex instead.
Generating or detonating a Wandering Vortex will also reduce nearby opponents' Anemo RES by 35% for 6s.
Additionally, nearby party members who enter the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state while Song of Ages Past is in effect will have the Radiance: Stellar Swirl state extended by 4s.

passives.name: Dirge of the Fandyr
passives.description:
When the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn is used, Vodyanitsa will also gain 25 stacks of Lead Vocal as well as 10 stacks of Chorus.
The two effects above last 30s each, and the stack count is refreshed when the Elemental Skill is used.

passives.name: Echoes Over the Frozen Lake
passives.description:
Holding the Elemental Skill outside of combat will cause Vodyanitsa to embody her true Water Imp form and swim for up to 10s at the cost of Stamina. Naturally, as a Water Imp, she can also move across the water's surface. Vodyanitsa will exit her Water Imp form when the Elemental Skill is used again, when the duration ends, or when all Stamina is depleted.
Additionally, while Vodyanitsa can swim faster, her Stamina consumption rate is also increased.

passives.name: Heartless Siren Song
passives.description: As the Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe, Vodyanitsa sings in person in place of playing an instrument.

constellations.name: Waters in Full Splendor
constellations.description: Each time Vodyanitsa triggers the healing effect of Song of Ages Past, it also increases the ATK of all nearby party members by 0.8% of her Max HP for 5s.

constellations.name: Echoes That Pierce the Snow
constellations.description:
When the Horn of Spring's Call from the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn attacks the opponent, Vodyanitsa gains the "Two Voices in Black and White" effect which increases the CRIT DMG from Hydro DMG and Cryo DMG dealt by the currently active party member by 50% for 5s.
If there is a Wandering Vortex present on the field or in the 5s after a Wandering Vortex explodes, the effect changes to: increases the CRIT DMG from Stellar Swirl reaction DMG caused by the currently active party member by 60% for 5s.
Additionally, the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn is enhanced as follows: the duration of the Song of Ages Past effect is extended by 9s.

constellations.name: Song Lingering on a Spring Morning
constellations.description:
Increases the Level of the Elemental Skill Rechitativ: Sonorous Dawn by 3.
Maximum upgrade level is 15.

constellations.name: Melancholic Voice Upon the Gentle Waters
constellations.description:
When Vodyanitsa triggers the healing effect of Song of Ages Past, an additional effect will be triggered based on the healed character's HP.
· If the character's HP is below 40%: The healing is increased by 50%; and
· If the character's HP is 40% or above: Vodyanitsa's Max HP is increased by 20% for 6s. Max 3 stacks, and each stack's duration is counted independently.

constellations.name: Together, Down Into the Deep
constellations.description:
Increases the Level of the Elemental Burst Koda: Sink With Thee by 3.
Maximum upgrade level is 15.

constellations.name: Neverending Song of Revelry
constellations.description:
The Constellation Echoes That Pierce the Snow is enhanced: "Two Voices in Black and White" now applies to all nearby party members.
Additionally, while the Song of Ages Past effect is active, Stellar Swirl reaction DMG dealt by nearby party members is elevated by 25% while Hydro DMG and Cryo DMG dealt are increased by 60%.

outfits.name: Surging Resonance
outfits.description:
Vodyanitsa's outfit. It is said to draw inspiration from various cultural traditions related to the Water Imps. For more details on these cultural elements, please direct them to Miss Vodyanitsa.
Of course, do wait until she is taking a break from her performances if you wish to ensure that she has time to spare.

voices.title: Hello
voices.text: Hello, I'm Vodyanitsa, the Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe. As you can see... Well, I mean, look at my ears. Pretty unusual, right? That's because I'm a "Water Imp." But that's neither here nor there. All you need to know is that I'm the best singer in the entire Korolevskiy Troupe.

voices.title: Chat: Hearing
voices.text: ...Hmm? Keep it down, I think I hear someone whispering again... Hehehe, lemme see if I can make out what they're saying...

voices.title: Chat: Practice
voices.text: Well, if there's nothing else going on, I might as well do some rehearsing... Uh, no, forget it. I don't wanna disturb the locals again. Or the animals...

voices.title: Chat: Passing the Time
voices.text: Whew... I've been on dry land for too long — my skin's getting dry. I'm in serious need of some underwater time.

voices.title: When It Rains
voices.text: Ah, what a lovely day. Perfect for some underwater relaxation.

voices.title: After the Rain
voices.text: Aw, where'd the rain go? What a downer...

voices.title: When It Snows
voices.text: A vast expanse of white. Hmph, if nothing else, it's a clean aesthetic.

voices.title: In the Desert
voices.text: Ugh, it's so hot and dry... Get me back to the water...

voices.title: Good Morning
voices.text: Good morning. I just finished my vocal warm-ups. Did you hear me? Yeah, I'm not surprised. My singing voice really carries.

voices.title: Good Afternoon
voices.text: Alright, time for some lunch. My poor voice is so tired after the morning I've had. I'll go get Odette, then we can grab a quick bite.

voices.title: Good Evening
voices.text: Whew, the day is finally over. I'm gonna take a dip in the lake in a bit, you wanna join me? ...Huh? What are you so scared of? Pssh, no, I don't drag people underwater and try to drown them! I'm not THAT kind of Water Imp! But I can do that if you want!

voices.title: Good Night
voices.text: Nighty-night~ You should get to bed — I'll be getting up pretty early tomorrow to do my vocal warm-ups. Of course, if you have any song requests, I'm more than happy to oblige.

voices.title: About Vodyanitsa: Charming Singing Voice
voices.text: Unfortunately, my voice doesn't cast any kind of magic spell on people that drives them crazy. People listen to me purely because I sing well. ...Ooh, although on that note, I actually have a joke about the Domovoy, hehehe... Ahem, never mind, forget I said that. Odette will start glaring at me again if I tell it.

voices.title: About Vodyanitsa: Scrutiny
voices.text: Whether you're a performer or not, if you truly want to be seen by other people, you have to accept the scrutiny that comes with it. Nothing worth having in this world comes without a price. And if it ever seems like you got something for free... Heh, that just means that fate has secretly decided the price for you.

voices.title: About Us: Fish Tail
voices.text: I turned my fish tail into two legs to make walking on land easier. ...What price did I pay? None! Hmph, for us Water Imps, leaving the water behind is a big enough price to pay already. What else do you wanna take away from me, the right to drink fresh water? I suppose you'd make me subsist entirely on fruit juice or Fonta, wouldn't you?

voices.title: About Us: Outing Days
voices.text: Still, I can't just stay in Snezhnaya all the time. Sometimes, I'll follow the waterways and swim around the world to hear what singers in other places sound like. I've been to Liyue, Fontaine, Inazuma, Sumeru... Huh? Has anyone ever noticed me? Hehe, of course. That's why there's legends about merfolk, mermaids, sirens, and so on all over the world. Natlan was something else, though... That place is hot. With a capital H, O, T.

voices.title: About the Vision
voices.text: Oh, this old thing? Yeah, it's pretty. Makes a nice piece of jewelry, I guess. But as a singer, I don't have much use for it most of the time. And as for "the gaze of the gods"... Hmph, I'm more interested in the gaze of my audience.

voices.title: Something to Share
voices.text: The water quality in Fontaine is amazing! Last time I traveled to Fontaine to watch a show, I couldn't resist diving underwater. I stayed there for ages, and gulped down loads of water. But I guess I must have made too much of a splash, because I caught the attention of someone from the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol who was training on the shore. She thought I was drowning... She came rushing to the rescue, yelling at the top of her lungs. But, uh... I just flicked my tail and whoosed away, hehehe. Then watched from a distance while she treaded water and looked around in confusion. It was pretty hilarious. Anyway, I waited until she was safely back on shore before I went underwater again to carry on gulping away. It really is delicious, you know. You should join me next time.

voices.title: Interesting Things
voices.text: Do you know about Frostfin Whales? They communicate using "whale songs," which most people can't even hear, let alone understand. But we Water Imps have no trouble understanding them, and we can even learn the language. I've actually gotten to know a Frostfin Whale named Hitova — real good-natured. Back when I was traveling all over, I hitched a ride off of her. I'll have to introduce you if I ever get the chance. I'm sure she'd be happy to take us both out for a ride.

voices.title: About Odette
voices.text: Whenever Odette is rehearsing, I listen along intently to her dance steps from backstage. She lands, then jumps, spins in the air, then lands again... Every motion is cleanly executed with impeccable timing. Just by listening, I can tell her dancing is flawless... Hm, why don't I go out front to watch? Hehe, because I wanna hide backstage and jump out at her afterwards! Sure, I haven't managed to scare her yet, but I have to keep trying. Otherwise, all that time I've spent hiding backstage would've been for nothing!

voices.title: About Mitya
voices.text: I wish that Mr. Smarty Pants would stop trying to make scientific breakthroughs while he's watching the show. The theater is not a glorified study hall, and it's certainly not a refugee camp for escaped office workers. He'd better start taking our performances seriously... or I'll be forced to... *sigh* What am I saying — there's nothing I can do about it, especially since he technically does abide by theater etiquette... Hmph, next time I see him in the audience, I'll have to perform one of my louder pieces. Let's see how well he can concentrate on his work then.

voices.title: About Alyosha
voices.text: I've always wondered if Alyosha's puppies can understand my songs. I'm guessing probably not, since we can't understand puppy songs either. Matter of fact, I don't even know if they can sing at all... But my lullabies work like a dream on them. I'll barely make it through the opening verse before they're all out like a light. ...Hmm, not sure what that says about my singing, though... Is that good or bad?

voices.title: About Vesna
voices.text: Thanks to Miss Vesna, those theater ticket scalpers know not to push their luck. She said she's planning to invite me to host a small conference on ticket scam prevention soon, and I'm supposed to be singing a song at the end to wrap things up. The thing is, out of all the songs I know, I don't think there's a single one for satirizing scam artists. ...Wait, tactical deception in war should count as a scam, right...? Ummm... maybe I could sing a war epic...?

voices.title: About Danica
voices.text: I'm not personally very familiar with Miss Danica, though of course, her reputation precedes her. She must have had it tough, answering to the Tsaritsa on one hand while having to deal with Miss Vesna on the other... Ahem, but uh, you didn't hear that. At least, not from me.

voices.title: About the Tsaritsa
voices.text: If Her Majesty the Tsaritsa comes to see a show at the theater, I'll break out the old songs of the Water Imps for her. ...How old? Well... Not so old that only the Tsaritsa has heard them before, but definitely old enough that you can hear the dust coming off when you start singing them. I just hope it doesn't get in people's eyes. Wouldn't want to make everyone cry.

voices.title: About Columbina
voices.text: Is Miss Columbina no longer a Harbinger? Huh, shame. I always thought she had a great singing voice. Her songs were like the moonlight itself: so soft and gentle, yet somehow icy cold. So present and vivid, yet so impossibly out of reach... Heh, I only hope she finds somewhere she can belong, with good friends who understand her songs.

voices.title: About Tartaglia
voices.text: Mr. Tartaglia often brings his family to the theater. Harbingers get free admission, although family members have to buy tickets like everyone else. Fortunately, he always manages to secure tickets for his family. Oh, right — you know Tonia, don't you? She's a huge theater fan. She might even join us when she grows up. If that happens, I guess Mr. Tartaglia will have to get used to visiting the theater even more often.

voices.title: About Arlecchino
voices.text: Lady Arlecchino sometimes brings a few children to watch a show at the theater. One of them has these cat ears — Lynette, I think her name was? Yeah, that's right — she and the boy, Lyney, are both excellent magicians. They actually performed a magic show here on the stage one time during an end-of-year performance. The only time Lady Arlecchino tends to come without the children is to watch "The Mountain Sparrow"... I suppose she prefers to enjoy that show alone.

voices.title: About Sandrone
voices.text: Miss Sandrone always seems to be in a hurry whenever she comes to see a show. Sometimes she grits her teeth, sometimes her eyes twitch... Other times, her face is completely blank, but she's crumpled some scrap paper into a ball. If I didn't know better, I'd say someone was forcing her to come against her will... But far be it from me to speculate who has the power to force her into anything. Still... Heh, she always seems a little more relaxed by the end of the show. So at least she's not completely wasting her time.

voices.title: About The Captain
voices.text: The captain? Oh, you mean THE Captain? Well... to be honest, I've never really had a proper conversation with him. I mean, we've exchanged a few brief words on occasion when we've bumped into each other after a show, but that's about it. Still, I can tell that he's a very serious and upstanding sort of person. Even in the audience stalls, he sits there completely straight, like a flagstaff or a pillar. I get the sense that nothing could ever faze him, let alone break him, not even the fiercest storm.

voices.title: More About Vodyanitsa: I
voices.text: So, you got some burning questions, huh? Well, ask away — but for every question you ask me, I get to ask you one, too. It's only fair. Don't worry, I won't ask any difficult questions. Just, uh... Y'know, the things I haven't found the answers to anywhere else.

voices.title: More About Vodyanitsa: II
voices.text: Sorry to burst your bubble, but we Snezhnayan Water Imps aren't some mythical creatures who drive sailors mad with our alluring songs, or pay some enormous price to walk on land, only to turn into sea foam if we break our vows. Nope, we're just ordinary people living ordinary lives, like everyone else in Snezhnaya.

voices.title: More About Vodyanitsa: III
voices.text: Since that incident, almost all the Water Imps have left Snezhnograd. My dear brothers and sisters invited me to leave with them, but I turned them down. I'm sure the citizens of Snezhnaya would be saddened if the day ever came that they could no longer hear our songs. And if Snezhnaya forgot our songs, the other Water Imps and I would be sad, too. That's why I stayed behind to keep singing. To prevent sadness all around.

voices.title: More About Vodyanitsa: IV
voices.text: ...Times have changed. Snezhnaya is a completely different place today. Inevitably, it's changed the way I relate to my singing, too. As time goes by, it's like the songs become... heavier, more layered and complex than ever, and I can't help but feel... Anyway, I don't like being like that, so I made a simple rule for myself: Whenever I feel like just going home, I find ten people in Snezhnaya and see if they like my singing. If even one out of ten genuinely likes my songs, I will stay. But if not even one person in ten cares, I'll return to my brothers and sisters.

voices.title: More About Vodyanitsa: V
voices.text: Heh, I don't know whether to call it good or bad luck, but every time I've sought out ten people to get their verdict, I've always found at least one who is genuinely willing to listen to my singing. Some were just starting out, others were deep in the trenches of the most heroic struggle of their lives, and some were calmly preparing for the final leg of their life's journey... Even if that were the entire audience, I and any of my kin who linger still in the theater would continue to sing for them. So, what about you? Do you enjoy my singing? Hehe. Be careful how you answer — we Water Imps have exceptionally good hearing. I'll know whether you're lying from your heartbeat alone. Ready? I'll count you in: Three, two...

voices.title: Vodyanitsa's Hobbies
voices.text: Whenever I'm in a good mood — or a really bad mood — I dive into the water, close my eyes, and let the current carry me around. As I drift along, I listen to all the sounds carried on the waves: Little fishies gathering together, their scales brushing against one another... giant whales singing deep, drawn-out songs as they call out to their partners far away... bubbles rising up from the deep, then bursting... Occasionally, when I drift by a city, I'll even hear the fishermen chanting as they cast their nets, children laughing as they leap into the water, and ships creaking as they prepare for a long voyage or return to port... Listening to the sounds of the world like this is truly magical. Do you want to try it? If so, I'll take you with me next time.

voices.title: Vodyanitsa's Troubles
voices.text: I don't like sounds laden with too much meaning. Singing is just another sound, like the news carried by the waves, the crisp sound of falling leaves, or the pitter-patter of running footsteps... The greater a sound's burden, the harder it is to understand, and the more unpleasant it is to my ear.

voices.title: Favorite Food
voices.text: Mm... Anything sweet, really. Although, preferably nice and cold, with just a dash of syrup, and... Huh, now that I say it out loud, I guess I'm just describing ice cream.

voices.title: Least Favorite Food
voices.text: If there's no moisture in it whatsoever, I just cannot handle it. I mean, I can physically force myself to swallow it, sure, but my throat will feel like it's being torn to shreds on the way down.

voices.title: Receiving a Gift: I
voices.text: Ooh, this is delicious! I guess you remembered what I told you about my favorite foods, huh? You have a pretty good memory. Next time, it's my turn to make some food tailored to your tastes. ...Yeah, I know you've never explicitly told me before, but don't worry — I already know. I have my ways of finding these things out.

voices.title: Receiving a Gift: II
voices.text: Thanks. Oh, by the way, do you still remember my favorite food? I told you last time. You do? Hmm... Guess you've got a pretty good memory. I'll have to give you something tougher to remember next time, hehehe.

voices.title: Receiving a Gift: III
voices.text: ...Maybe next time, I should be clear about my food preferences in advance. Or maybe I can teach you how to make something really delicious.

voices.title: Birthday
voices.text: Happy Birthday! I've set aside your gift. You can open it later. It's just some small trinkets, toys, and whatnot... Eh, but that's not the important part. You're free now, aren't you? In that case, come with me! We're going to my echo chamber. I got someone to buy me a Dance-Off Stage from Natlan a few days ago, along with a whole bunch of weird and wonderful instruments. I'm working on the best music event Snezhnaya's ever seen, and guess who's the first person to receive an invitation? That's right, it's you! Come on, let's sing the night away!

voices.title: Feelings About Ascension: Intro
voices.text: Ahem, ahem... Alright. Sounding good.

voices.title: Feelings About Ascension: Building Up
voices.text: I think I just reached a new high note.

voices.title: Feelings About Ascension: Climax
voices.text: Ah, my voice is feeling stronger than ever.

voices.title: Feelings About Ascension: Conclusion
voices.text: Whoo! Time to sing the whole night through!

voices.title: Elemental Skill: I
voices.text: Listen closely.

voices.title: Elemental Skill: II
voices.text: Start with a warm up.

voices.title: Elemental Skill: III
voices.text: Taking the stage.

voices.title: Elemental Skill: IV
voices.text: This is more like it...

voices.title: Elemental Skill: V
voices.text: Heehee, look at my fish tail!

voices.title: Elemental Skill: VI
voices.text: Woo! Hahahaha!

voices.title: Elemental Burst: I
voices.text: An elegy to mortality.

voices.title: Elemental Burst: II
voices.text: An ode to eras past.

voices.title: Elemental Burst: III
voices.text: Everyone, lift your voices!

voices.title: Opening Treasure Chest: I
voices.text: Wow! Look at all these shiny treasures! Quick, grab 'em!

voices.title: Opening Treasure Chest: II
voices.text: This looks alright, I guess. Could be fun to play around with.

voices.title: Opening Treasure Chest: III
voices.text: Is that it? Huh. So much for "treasure" chest...

voices.title: Low HP: I
voices.text: Hehe... Heh...

voices.title: Low HP: II
voices.text: I'm done playing.

voices.title: Low HP: III
voices.text: ...Oh, you'll regret that.

voices.title: Ally at Low HP: I
voices.text: Hey! What are you doing!?

voices.title: Ally at Low HP: II
voices.text: Get over here! Stop messing around!

voices.title: Fallen: I
voices.text: You're all here...

voices.title: Fallen: II
voices.text: Waves... carry me home...

voices.title: Fallen: III
voices.text: A high note... to end on...

voices.title: Light Hit Taken: I
voices.text: I slipped...

voices.title: Light Hit Taken: II
voices.text: Hmph! I'm not done yet...!

voices.title: Heavy Hit Taken: I
voices.text: Face me in the water if you're so tough!

voices.title: Heavy Hit Taken: II
voices.text: I'm not built for dry land...!

voices.title: Joining Party: I
voices.text: My ears are burning.

voices.title: Joining Party: II
voices.text: Here I am. What's up?

voices.title: Joining Party: III
voices.text: *clear throat* Mm, my vocal cords are all warmed up.
